Having flexible binding.
To issue or publish (a book) in a paperback edition.

examples.text: Max was anticipating paperbacking The Bodley Head's books in house rather than licensing the paperback rights to a third party, like Penguin, which reduced his royalties and might eventually lose him authors to vertical publishers.

glosses: Having the sort of flexible binding characteristic of a paperback book.

examples.text: He has literary leanings, is reading Gibbon's Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, buying each volume as he can, in a paperbacked edition.

glosses: Having the sort of binding characteristic of a softcover book.

examples.text: Our reviewer Kai T. Erikson remarked that Michael Brown's book, updated for this softcovered edition, "does what good reporting should do—alert us, educate us, provide a focus for our apprehension, plainly and clearly."

glosses: Having flexible covers; paperback; softcovered.

examples.text: Last week in collaboration with his longtime associate, Frederick Shelton, Editor Kiplinger published a paperbound booklet called Inflation Ahead!—What to do about it.

glosses: Involving or burdened by excessive administrative requirements, especially in the form of paperwork.

examples.text: The company has turned to In Touch to automate what had been a paperbound process.
“We need to bring this paperbound system into the 21st century,” he said.

glosses: A paperback book.

examples.text: Few book budgets can stretch enough to provide for the desired duplicates, but the paperbounds cost so little that by using them heavy duplication is possible. We also find them useful for duplication of titles that have only occasional demand.

glosses: Qui est broché, qui a une broche, qui est travaillé au brochoir.

examples.text: Il y eut des articles sur le Complexe Webuy dans la plupart des publications spécialisées à travers le monde, il serait étonnant que le plus petit paquet de feuilles brochées par quelque association étudiante de Nouvelle-Zélande n’ait pas fait paraître son propre compte rendu.

glosses: Se dit d’un livre assemblé par collage de la tranche des feuillets au dos de sa couverture, qui est souple.
target_senses.note: Initialement, le « brochage » désignait le fait de coudre les cahiers à la main ; c’est avec l’automatisation au début du xxᵉ siècle que la « brocheuse » a désigné la machine à coller les pages

examples.text: Les livres brochés coûtent souvent moins que les reliés.
Le relieur reçoit l’ouvrage broché ; son premier travail consiste à en décoller la couverture, et à débrocher les cahiers.

glosses: Participe passé masculin singulier du verbe brocher.

examples.text: Foi de journaliste, j’ai broché plus de cent articles contre les auteurs de qui vous parlez ; mais j’avoue que, si je les ai attaqués, c’était pour dire quelque chose qui ressemblât à de la critique.
